newsitem.title: LEBANON: U.S. companies long to return to Lebanon - minister.
newsitem.headline: U.S. companies long to return to Lebanon - minister.

text.p: U.S. companies, barred from coming to Lebanon by a U.S. travel ban, are longing to return to have a slice of the postwar reconstruction process, Lebanon's Economy Minister Yassin Jaber was quoted on Tuesday as saying.
"American companies are longing to return to Lebanon to take part in the ongoing construction process," Jaber told the Christian Beirut daily newspaper Nida'a al-Watan in an interview.

Jaber, who attended a December 16 international conference in Washington for countries interested in donating aid to Lebanon, said the ban, in force since 1985, was not justified and the Lebanese government was seeking to have it lifted.
"I do not see any political justifications for the ban any more. There may be a security justification which we are striving through co-operation and agreement to solve," Jaber added.
The United States imposed a travel ban on Lebanon when Moslem guerrillas hijacked a TWA airliner to Beirut in 1985 and killed an American passenger on board.
President Bill Clinton said as the Washington meeting was in progress that the ban would be maintained since it was still not safe for American businessmen to travel to Lebanon at present.

The donors' conference has pledged $3.2 billion in loans and donations to Lebanon to help it recover from the 1975-90 civil war. The United States has said that its aid to Lebanon would rise to $12 million in 1997 from $2 million in 1996.
